title: Session token oddities and 401/429 debugging notes
content:
Observed behavior:
- Intermittent 401s from long-running background job (worker-sync) starting 2025-02-18 18:14 PST.
- Periodic 429 spikes during bursts from UI e2e tests and replication job.
- 401s correlate with immediate token rotation events seen in auth logs.

Timeline:
2025-02-18 17:58 PST - deploy: background job updated (git sha abc123).
2025-02-18 18:14 PST - first 401 observed in worker logs: "invalid_api_key".
2025-02-19 09:03 PST - load test run -> many 429s, Retry-After header alternating between 5 and 0.
2025-02-20 11:21 PST - temporarily fixed by reloading credentials in k8s secret.

Commands tried:
- curl with explicit token:
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
- curl showing header whitespace:
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY " https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- base64/length check:
echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY" | wc -c
- token rotate (kubectl):
kubectl create secret generic redwood-api-key --from-literal=key="$NEW_KEY" -n infra && kubectl rollout restart deploy/worker-sync

Sample responses (copied):
401:
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"unauthorized","message":"API key invalid or revoked","code":"invalid_api_key"}

429:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":12,"message":"token bucket exhausted"}

Observations:
- 401s often follow a short window of successful requests for same key -> suggests transient revocation or race during rotation.
- 429s include consistent Retry-After but sometimes header missing (0 or absent) -> client SDK didn't backoff properly.
- Some 401s contained a subtle error: server logs show "malformed token" where incoming token had trailing newline (likely env injection or secret mount issue).

Hypotheses:
- Secret injection on k8s mounts sometimes adds newline (we saw in env var length check +1).
- There's a race between key rotation script and distributed workers reading secret; some pods read older key while rotation marks old key as revoked.
- Rate limit counters are per-tenant but SDK uses per-second bursts leading to token bucket exhaustion when many parallel requests.
- Time skew on some hosts caused signed tokens (if using JWT) to be briefly invalid (check NTP sync).

What fixed it temporarily:
- Restarting pods to force reload of secret removed 401s for ~4h.
- Adding client-side jitter/backoff reduced 429 occurrence in spike tests.

Next steps / TODO:
- Add instrumentation to auth service to log truncated token lengths and request-id (INF-logs RWI-1299).
- Update rotation script to write new key with a 'grace' period: keep old key valid for 5m after publish.
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter in SDK for 429s (see repository: github.com/redwood/sdk#retry-policy).
- Audit k8s secret mounts for processes that might echo key with newline (check init containers).
- Add alert when X-RateLimit-Remaining <= 5 for any key (<-- Alert rule draft).

Notes & references:
- Slack thread: https://slack.com/archives/C01AUTH123/p163... (see Evan's message 2025-02-19)
- Related ticket: RWI-1234 (investigate 401 bursts during rotation)
- PR that changed rotation: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/582
- Auth docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/auth#api-keys

Scratch ideas:
- Add probe endpoint that returns hashed token fingerprint so we can check which pods have which key without exposing token.
- Local reproducer: small script that rotates key every 2m and blasts requests from 50 parallel workers.

Quick reproducer (bash):
for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/echo & done; wait

End.
